XIII.}}}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=13|verse=6}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel on the Imber Saturday in Sept.}}And he {{ls}}aid this {{ls}}imilitude, A certaine man had {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The figtree vvith only leaues & no fruite, is the Iewes {{ls}}ynagogue, & euery other people or per{{ls}}on which hath faith and faire wordes, and no good workes.}}∷ a figtree planted in his vineyard, and he came {{ls}}eeking for fruite on it, and found not. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=7}} And he {{ls}}aid to the dre{{ls}}{{ls}}er of the vineyard, Loe it is three yeres {{ls}}ince I come {{ls}}eeking for fruite vpon this figtree: and I finde not. Cut it dovvne therfore: vvhereto doth it al{{ls}}o occupie the ground? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=8}} But he an{{ls}}wering {{ls}}aith to him, Lord, let it alone this yere al{{ls}}o, vntil I digge about it, and dung it. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=9}} and if happily it yeld fruite: but if not, hereafter thou {{ls}}halt cut it dovvne.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=10}} And he vvas teaching in their {{ls}}ynagogue on the Sabboths. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=11}} And behold a vvoman that had a {{ls}}pirit of infirmitie eightene yeres: and {{ls}}he vvas crooked neither could {{ls}}he looke vpvvard at al. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=12}} Whom vvhen {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}avv, he called her vnto him, and {{ls}}aid to her, Woman, thou art deliuered from thy infirmitie. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=13}} And he impo{{ls}}ed hands vpon her, and forthvvith {{ls}}he vvas made {{ls}}traight and glorified God. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=14}} And the Arch{{ls}}ynagogue an{{ls}}vvering (becau{{ls}}e he had indignation that {{sc|Iesvs}} had cured on the Sabboth) {{ls}}aid to the multitude, Sixe daies there are vvherein you ought to vvorke. in them therfore come, and be cured: and not in the Sabboth day. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=15}} And our Lord an{{ls}}vvering to him, {{ls}}aid, Hypocrite, doth not euery one of you vpon the Sabboth loo{{ls}}e his oxe or his a{{ls}}{{ls}}e from the manger, and leadeth them to vvater? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=16}} But {{sup|‖}} this daughter of Abraham vvhom Satan hath bound, loe, the{{ls}}e eightene yeres, ought not {{ls}}he to be loo{{ls}}ed from this bond on the Sabboth day? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=17}} And vvhen he {{ls}}aid the{{ls}}e things, al his aduer{{ls}}aries vvere a{{ls}}hamed: and al the people reioyced in al things that vvere gloriou{{ls}}ly done of him.⊣

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=18}} He {{ls}}aid therfore, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 13, 31. Mr. 4, 30.''}}* VVherevnto is the kingdom of God like, and vvherevnto {{ls}}hal I e{{ls}}teeme it like? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=19}} It is like to a {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ See Annota. Matth. ''13, 31''.}}∷ mu{{ls}}tard {{ls}}eede, vvhich a man tooke and ca{{ls}}t into his garden, and it grevv: and became a great tree, and the foules of the aire re{{ls}}ted in the boughes thereof. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=20}} And againe he {{ls}}aid, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 13, 33.''}}* Like to vvhat {{ls}}hal I e{{ls}}teeme the kingdom of God? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=21}} It is like to leauen, vvhich a vvoman tooke and hid in three mea{{ls}}ures of meale, til the vvhole vvas leauened. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=22}} And he vvent by cities and tovvnes teaching, and making his iourney vnto Hieru{{ls}}alem.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=23}} And a certaine man {{ls}}aid to him, Lord, be they fevv that are {{ls}}aued? {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 7, 13.''}}* But he {{ls}}aid to them, {{verse|chapter=13|verse=24}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Chri{{ls}}tians in their liues mu{{ls}}t {{ls}}eeke the {{ls}}trait way, but in religion the ancient common way.}}∷ Striue to enter {{sup|‖}} by the narrow gate: becau{{ls}}e many, I {{ls}}ay to you, {{sup|‖}} {{ls}}hal {{ls}}eeke to enter,<noinclude>{{continues|and}}</noinclude>
